A1.justification: Both PDFs describe gp2Scale, with matching method sections and benchmark experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and all appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original predictive experiments on five datasets in Tables 1–5 and computational scaling measurements in Appendix B.6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally presents topography posterior predictions and uncertainties in Appendix E, Figure 4.

M1.justification: Equation (3) changes the specified Wendland kernel's cubic coefficient from 35 to 32. The kernel constructions, distributed computation, and block-MCMC framework otherwise remain; expanded appendix descriptions do not establish additional algorithm changes or changed implementations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic function, topography, California housing, MNIST, temperature, and synthetic timing datasets/tasks. The new topography prediction grid extends analysis within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within corresponding experiments: SVGP, VNNGP, SKI, and Vecchia where applicable, plus the base GP for the synthetic example. The same unavailable comparisons remain marked NA.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes Vecchia's stated fitting procedure from MCMC to MLE-II; this revises the reported protocol without establishing that experiments were rerun. New Figure 4 evaluates topography predictions on a 100-by-100 grid. Existing benchmark splits, budgets, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E and Figure 4 add a qualitative topography case study examining recovered terrain structure and spatially varying predictive uncertainty. The kernel-selection and MCMC guidance adds explanations, not controlled ablations or sensitivity experiments.

E5.justification: Appendix B revises the reported statistical estimation procedure for Vecchia from MCMC to MLE-II and explicitly describes gp2Scale's MCMC as propagating hyperparameter uncertainty. Reporting of means and standard deviations across ten runs, with one run for the temperature experiment, remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Appendix B.6 changes LOGDET time from 6.97306 to 1.06100 for 200,000 points at sparsity 6.40E-04, retaining total time 18.9802. Figure 4 adds topography posterior results. All numerical benchmark results in Tables 1–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Besides the coefficient revision in Equation (3), Section 4.3 corrects the expansion of g(xi)g(xj) to use b(xi,xp)b(xj,xq), replacing the repeated unspecified x arguments. These are limited mathematical corrections; Appendix A's theorem and proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims about exact GP scaling to ten million points, sparsity-discovering kernels, customization flexibility, and competitive predictive performance.

C2.justification: New Appendix C.3 explains dataset-specific kernel choices, while Appendix D discusses blocking and prior tradeoffs. Section 5 acknowledges potentially stronger baseline extensions, and the Impact Statement discusses resource costs. Figure 4 adds a spatial uncertainty interpretation without changing the central applicability conclusions.

D1.justification: Reproducibility documentation expands substantially: Appendix B.7 supplies practical DASK scheduling, 15,000-point A100 block guidance, and caching details; Appendix D specifies hyperparameter blocking, normal proposals, and prior recommendations. The reproducibility statement replaces a promised future release with a specific repository address and data-access instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning remain the same. Hensman's and Higdon's references receive publication metadata updates for the same works, rather than representing added research.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language, author-information, acknowledgment, and reference edits, and adds explanatory appendix sections and an Impact Statement. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact; former Appendix C.3 is retained as C.4.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format, with reformatted equations, resized figures, and relocated tables, including grouping Tables 2–5 together. Figures 1–3 retain their underlying content; Figure 4 is newly added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves practical usability through concrete code/data access instructions and clearer kernel-selection, distributed-computing, and MCMC guidance. Corrected mathematical indexing and the internally consistent timing entry improve precision. The main benchmark evidence remains unchanged, and the useful new topography visualization does not independently establish its calibration interpretation, limiting the overall gain.
